newsitem.title: USA: US foreign crude trade enters pre-holday slumber.
newsitem.headline: US foreign crude trade enters pre-holday slumber.

text.p: Activity in markets for foreign crude for delivery into the U.S. Gulf slowed to a trickle ahead of the three-day U.S. Memorial Day weekend, with the delay of a Cusiana tender to show for it, traders said.
"The slowness started in London, now it's come here. Tomorrow should be a dead day," said one trader.

At least one cargo changed hands as a European trading house sold a cargo for July 1-5 U.S. Gulf arrival at a $1.93 premium to Dated Brent, which amounts to about a 10 cents premium over July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.

Meanwhile Colombia's state-owned Ecopetrol, frustrated at low levels of bids on its latest Cusiana tender, was heard to have pushed back the loading date to June 23-24 from the previous June 17-18 window.

Traders said that unless a "Cusiana savior" like a U.S. major swooped in and bid at a price attractive to Ecopetrol, chances were that downward pressure on the cargo were enough to push the price well below the $1.23 discount to July WTI/Cushing British Petroleum closed on Monday.
Most players regarded the emerging softness lightly, saying the U.S. holiday and the transition between the June and July cargo markets would soon come to a close.
In other activity, the same European trading house that sold the Qua Iboe was heard to be offering a Brent cargo for July 1-5 arrival into the U.S. Gulf at a 70 cents discount to July WTI/Cushing.
But some traders said that price was steadily moving higher as bids have come in, which has cast suspicion on the veracity of the whole cargo offering.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk, 1 212 859 1633
